title: The Gravity of the Rust Belt
premise: Ivo Fairweather, a xenolinguist whose mind was rewired by contact with an alien signal, has spent years in self-imposed exile maintaining a decommissioned beacon on the edge of the Rust Belt, a graveyard of failed colonies. When a name from their past appears on the manifest of a ship that officially never flew, Ivo realizes someone is hunting everyone who ever heard the original transmission. Forced out of hiding, Ivo gathers a ragtag crew of fellow erased people and races toward the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the truth before the corporation behind the cover-up can erase the last witnesses. At the relay, Ivo must choose between destroying the evidence that could save their crew but cost them their own humanity, or letting the signal through and finally dreaming in a language no human was meant to know. They let it through, sacrificing their old self, and the found family they built carries what remains of them home.
about_author: G. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining transmission towers across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. Their work blends working-class grit with deep-space melancholy, and they write exclusively at night, when the signals come in clearest.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Commissioned
chapters.summary: Ivo Fairweather's POV. Ivo maintains the derelict beacon in the Rust Belt, speaking aloud in a language they invented and no longer dreaming in human tongues. A routine manifest check reveals an impossible name: Sefa Okonkwo, listed on the Perihelion, a ship that never flew. The emotional beat is the first crack in Ivo's carefully maintained invisibility, and the fear that follows.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Perihelion
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Digging through corrupted shipping records, Ivo confirms Sefa was their old crewmate from the original listening expedition, presumed dead for eleven years. The name is a breadcrumb, or bait. A corporate survey vessel enters the sector, scanning derelicts. Ivo must decide whether to run or investigate. The beat is paranoia sharpening into resolve: someone is pulling the dead back into the light.

chapters.title: People the Paperwork Ate
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with interludes from dockworker-turned-smuggler Rhea Vance. Ivo descends into the Rust Belt's black-market station, Halcyon Yard, seeking Rhea, who once ferried erased people to safety. Rhea recognizes the name Perihelion and reveals three others on the manifest are alive, scattered, and hiding. The beat is the first fragile formation of a found family out of shared erasure.

chapters.title: What the Signal Taught Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Ivo's POV, framed as a recorded testimony Ivo prepares in case they don't survive. Ivo recounts the original expedition: first contact with the signal, the corporation's order to suppress it, and the neural rewiring that let Ivo understand it at the cost of human dreaming. The beat is grief for the self Ivo lost, and the dawning truth that Sefa may have survived the same procedure.

chapters.title: The Long Way Through Dead Space
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating between Ivo, Rhea, and salvager Dez Okoro, the third name on the manifest. The crew assembles a patched-together ship and plots a course to the relay through dead space, where no rescue exists. Corporate hunters pick up their trail. The beat is loyalty tested under pressure: each member must choose the crew over their own survival odds.

chapters.title: Sefa
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The crew intercepts a distress ping and finds Sefa Okonkwo alive aboard a drifting hulk, half-wired into the ship's systems, dreaming the alien signal continuously. Sefa reveals the corporation isn't hiding the signal, they're feeding it, using rewired minds as living antennas. The beat is reunion shadowed by horror: the person Ivo came to save may no longer be fully a person.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rhea's POV. A corporate boarding party cripples the ship, and someone aboard fed them the route. Evidence points to Dez, but Rhea discovers the real leak is Sefa, broadcasting involuntarily through her implants. Rhea must choose: tell the crew and risk Ivo abandoning Sefa, or lie to protect the fragile family. The beat is loyalty versus truth, and Rhea's choice to lie, for now.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge of Nothing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The crew reaches the relay, a cathedral of dead antennas at the boundary of dead space, with corporate ships closing in. Sefa's condition deteriorates; the signal is burning her out. The only way to expose the corporation is to let the full signal through the relay, but it will overwrite any mind tuned to receive it, and Ivo's rewired brain is the only receiver that works. The beat is dread and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Dreaming in the Alien Tongue
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, dissolving into second person as the signal takes hold. Ivo plugs into the relay and opens the channel, experiencing the signal whole: not an invasion but a message, a record of a civilization's end, offered freely. Corporate ships arrive to find the truth already propagating across every network. The beat is transcendence and self-annihilation braided together; Ivo lets their old self go.

chapters.title: The Weight We Carry Home
chapters.summary: Rhea's POV. Ivo survives but no longer speaks any human language fluently; the crew becomes their translators, their tether, their family. The broadcast topples the corporation's cover-up, and the erased are named, mourned, and remembered. Rhea brings Ivo home to Halcyon Yard, where the beacon still hums. The beat is bittersweet resolution: justice outside the law, truth at terrible cost, and a family that refuses to let go.
